kings1.13.p1.b1.text: Suddenly, as Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense, there came a man of God from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD.

kings1.13.p1.b2.text: “O altar, O altar, this is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David, and upon you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you…’”

kings1.13.p1.b3.text: “The LORD has spoken this sign: ‘Surely the altar will be split apart, and the ashes upon it will be poured out.’”

kings1.13.p2.b2.text: But the hand he stretched out toward him withered, so that he could not pull it back.

kings1.13.p2.b3.text: And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

kings1.13.p2.b4.text: “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray that my hand may be restored.”

kings1.13.p3.b1.text: “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”

kings1.13.p3.b2.text: “If you were to give me half your possessions, I still would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.

kings1.13.p3.b3.text: For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”

kings1.13.p3.b4.text: So the man of God went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.

kings1.13.p4.b1.text: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man had spoken to the king.

kings1.13.p4.b4.text: “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?”

kings1.13.p5.b1.text: “Come home with me and eat some bread.”

kings1.13.p5.b2.text: “I cannot return with you… For I have been told by the word of the LORD…”

kings1.13.p5.b3.text: “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’”

kings1.13.p5.b4.text: The old prophet was lying to him…

kings1.13.p6.b1.text: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,

kings1.13.p6.b2.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God gave you, but you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where He told you not to do so, your body shall never reach the tomb of your fathers.’”

kings1.13.p7.b1.text: And after the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.

kings1.13.p7.b2.text: As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road…

kings1.13.p7.b3.text: And his body was left lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

kings1.13.p7.b4.text: And there were men passing by who saw the body lying in the road… and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.

kings1.13.p8.b1.text: “It is the man of God who disobeyed the command of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion… according to the word that the LORD had spoken to him.”

kings1.13.p8.b2.text: and he went and found the body lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.

kings1.13.p8.b3.text: Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they lamented over him,

kings1.13.p9.b1.text: “When I die, you must bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones,

kings1.13.p9.b2.text: For the message that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel… will surely come to pass.”

kings1.13.p9.b3.text: Even after these events, Jeroboam did not repent of his evil ways… He ordained anyone who desired to be a priest of the high places.

kings1.13.p9.b4.text: And this was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its extermination and destruction from the face of the earth.
